title: Numbers, money & shopping
intro:
Japan's currency is the yen ({円[えん]}). Coins come in 1, 5, 10, 50, 100 and 500 yen; common notes are 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 yen (a 2,000-yen note exists but is rare). New banknote designs were introduced in 2024, and older notes remain valid.

Japanese counts large numbers in units of ten thousand ({万[まん]}), not thousands. So 10,000 is {一万[いちまん]}, 50,000 is {五万[ごまん]}, and 120,000 is {十二万[じゅうにまん]}. Rents and salaries are almost always quoted this way, so practice it until it is automatic.

Prices shown to consumers must include consumption tax, so the big number on the tag is usually what you pay ({税込[ぜいこみ]}). You may also see the pre-tax price ({税抜[ぜいぬき]}) in smaller print. Food bought to take away is taxed at a lower rate than eating in.

Cash is still widely used, but card, IC-card and QR-code payments are now common in cities. Smaller shops and restaurants may still be cash only, so keep some cash on you.

At the register, put your money in the small tray rather than handing it directly to the cashier, and receive your change the same way or by hand. Plastic shopping bags cost a few yen, so you will be asked if you need one. Note that tax-free shopping is for short-term visitors; once you live in Japan you are generally not eligible.

phrases.jp: 全部[ぜんぶ]でいくらですか。

phrases.note: For example {電池[でんち]はどこにありますか} (Where are the batteries?).

phrases.jp: もう少[すこ]し大[おお]きいサイズはありますか。
phrases.en: Do you have a slightly bigger size?

phrases.jp: 試着[しちゃく]してもいいですか。
カードは使[つか]えますか。
現金[げんきん]でお願[ねが]いします。
一括[いっかつ]払[ばら]いでお願[ねが]いします。
phrases.note: When you pay by credit card, staff may ask how many installments you want. {一括[いっかつ]} (one payment) is the normal answer.

phrases.jp: 袋[ふくろ]はいりません。
領収書[りょうしゅうしょ]をお願[ねが]いします。
phrases.note: A {領収書[りょうしゅうしょ]} is the official receipt used for work expense claims. Staff will ask who to make it out to ({宛名[あてな]}).

phrases.jp: 一万円[いちまんえん]からお願[ねが]いします。
phrases.en: Here's ten thousand yen. (please take it out of this)

phrases.jp: 返品[へんぴん]できますか。
ポイントカードはお持[も]ちですか。
phrases.en: Do you have a point card? (staff)
phrases.note: You will hear this constantly. {持[も]っていません} or simply {大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です} is fine.

tips: Learn to hear prices in units of {万[まん]}: 75,000 yen is {七万五千円[ななまんごせんえん]}. Practice by reading rent listings aloud.
Use the money tray at the register. Placing cash in it is the normal, polite way to pay.
Carry a reusable bag. Plastic bags are charged in almost all shops.
Keep receipts for work purchases, and ask for a {領収書[りょうしゅうしょ]} when your company will reimburse you.
Shop staff speak very polite Japanese ({ございます}, {いただけます}). You only need to answer in normal {です／ます}.
